what_changed_recently.headline: Rights Issue Call Money Realization & Equity Conversion Complete
what_changed_recently.detail: Bharti Airtel completed the final call money collection on rights issue partly paid-up equity shares, receiving ₹15,696 Cr in call money and converting 460,340 shares to fully paid equity, significantly strengthening its balance sheet.

what_changed_recently.headline: India Mobile ARPU Reaches ₹264 Driven by Postpaid Record Additions
what_changed_recently.detail: India mobile ARPU expanded to ₹264 in Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter), supported by tariff adjustments, Fast Lane network slicing adoption, and a record 1.0 million postpaid customer additions in a single quarter.

what_changed_recently.headline: Airtel Money NBFC Licensing & Planned London Listing
what_changed_recently.detail: Airtel Money Ltd secured RBI approval for a Type II NBFC license to scale proprietary digital lending via Airtel Finance, while preparing Airtel Money for a London listing in H2 2026.

growth_drivers.driver_title: Nxtra Data Center Expansion to 1 GW Capacity
growth_drivers.description: Nxtra Data Centers is executing a massive capacity expansion plan from 120-220 MW towards 1 GW over the coming years, securing prime land parcels in Mumbai and stitching contracts with global hyperscalers like Google.
growth_drivers.execution_status: Active land acquisition and construction phase; 120 MW under active build
growth_drivers.expected_impact: Captures high-margin data center colocation and AI cloud hosting demand across India.
growth_drivers.source_quote: Nxtra Data Limited (data centre arm) also reported strong 17% revenue growth led by capacity augmentation. During the year, the company announced large-scale expansion in its data centre business, with plans to build 1 GW of capacity over the coming years.

growth_drivers.description: Scaling home broadband reach through a dual FTTH and 5G Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) strategy, expanding FTTH to 43 Million home passes and AirFiber to 3,300+ cities to reach 25 Million connected homes.
growth_drivers.stated_outlay_or_value: Accelerated fiber and transport layer capital allocation
growth_drivers.execution_status: Customer base reached 14.2M in FY26 following record 4.2M annual net additions.
growth_drivers.expected_impact: Drives recurring high-ARPU subscription revenue and reduces churn via converged One Airtel plans.
growth_drivers.source_quote: FY 2025-26 marked an inflection point for the Homes Broadband segment business. Net additions stood at a record high of 4.2 million, taking the customer base to 14.2 million. FWA continued to expand the addressable market, with Airtel’s offerings now live in over 3,300 cities.

growth_drivers.description: Integrating Airtel Money's new NBFC lending capabilities with Airtel Payments Bank's 120M monthly transacting users under the Airtel Finance storefront to offer personal loans, co-branded credit products, and digital savings.
growth_drivers.target_timeline: Live in Q1 FY27, rapidly scaling monthly run-rates
growth_drivers.execution_status: Lending live; Payments Bank annualized revenue run rate crossed ₹3,400 Cr.
growth_drivers.expected_impact: High-margin financial services monetization across Airtel's 373M+ Indian subscriber ecosystem.
growth_drivers.source_quote: Airtel Payments bank, which is another engine of our financial services portfolio, continues to deliver strong performance. We ended Q1 with a monthly transacting user base of around 120 million. The annualized revenue run rate is now over Rs.3400 Crores

promise_vs_delivery.management_promise: Promised aggressive balance sheet deleveraging by prepaying high-cost spectrum liabilities and reducing Net Debt / EBITDA below 2.0x.
promise_vs_delivery.promise_quote: We prepaid C251,244 million of high-cost spectrum liabilities in FY 2024-25, taking our cumulative prepaid spectrum liabilities to C658,083 million in the last four years... improving our net debt-to-EBITDAaL ratio to 2.1x.
promise_vs_delivery.actual_outcome: Delivered substantial deleveraging with Net Debt to EBITDAaL declining to 1.3x by end of FY26 and 0.7x (ex-leases) in Q1 FY27, retiring ₹300,305 million in net debt YoY.
promise_vs_delivery.actual_quote: On a reported basis, net debt declined by H300,305 million year-on-year, improving Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio to 1.3x at end of March 2026 vs 2.1x at the end of March 2025.
promise_vs_delivery.stocker_analysis: Management exceeded its leverage reduction guidance ahead of schedule through strong operating cash flows and call money proceeds from the rights issue.
promise_vs_delivery.financial_numbers_check: Reported audited financial statements show borrowings dropped from ₹213,642 Cr in FY25 to ₹195,412 Cr in FY26 (a reduction of ₹18,230 Cr), while Operating Cash Flow (CFO) surged from ₹98,332 Cr to ₹122,230 Cr (up 24.3% YoY).

promise_vs_delivery.management_promise: Guided towards organic ARPU expansion past ₹215 and upwards to ₹245-250 through tariff repair, 2G to 4G/5G upgrades, and postpaid premiumization.
promise_vs_delivery.promise_quote: We have achieved an industry-leading ARPU of C245, a Y-o-Y increase of C36. This strong revenue growth was supported by an improved portfolio mix, continued premiumisation and tariff repair
promise_vs_delivery.actual_outcome: ARPU reached ₹257 in FY26 and further expanded to ₹264 in Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter).
promise_vs_delivery.actual_quote: Our ARPU for the quarter came in at Rs.264, which also had the benefit of an extra day during the quarter.
promise_vs_delivery.stocker_analysis: ARPU growth guidance has been consistently delivered through disciplined execution on premiumization and tariff pass-through without market share loss.
promise_vs_delivery.financial_numbers_check: Quarterly sales expanded from ₹47,876 Cr in Mar 2025 to ₹58,539 Cr in Jun 2026 (up 22.3% in 5 quarters), directly driven by ARPU expansion while quarterly OPM held firm at 57.0%.

demand_momentum.summary: Demand momentum across Airtel's ecosystem is robust, supported by ongoing 5G upgrades, strong postpaid adoption, rapid broadband expansion, and digital enterprise transformation. Per-user data consumption remains elevated at 28.3 GB/month, while B2B digital services (Cloud, IoT, Cybersecurity) and Airtel Payments Bank are compounding at double-digit growth rates.

segment_trends.trend: +13.2% YoY revenue growth; ARPU expanded to ₹264 with 1.0M postpaid net adds in Q1 FY27.
+30.2% YoY revenue growth; customer base reached 14.2M with 4.2M net adds in FY26.
+12% YoY revenue growth in Q1 FY27 to ₹5,670 Cr, led by Cloud, IoT, and SD-WAN deal wins.
+24.2% YoY constant currency revenue growth; Airtel Money revenues up 30.1% CC.

demand_momentum.market_share_and_pricing: Sustained market share leadership in premium accounts (>₹500/month ARPU) at ~42%. Completed headline tariff adjustments with minimal churn (<1.8%). ARPU expanded steadily to ₹264.
headwinds_and_risks: Cost inflation in FWA CPE equipment due to elevated memory and chipset prices.
Foreign currency exchange volatility across African subsidiaries (e.g. Nigerian Naira).
Softness in entry-level 2G voice segment requiring subscriber migration support.
demand_momentum.source_quote: Our ARPU for the quarter came in at Rs.264... We added 1 million postpaid customers this quarter, which is the highest ever addition in any quarter for us.

risks_and_cash.working_capital_and_receivables: Trade receivables are well-managed across a diversified B2C and B2B base with standard credit terms of 14-30 days for mobile and 7-90 days for Airtel Business. Operating Cash Flow (CFO) reached a record ₹122,230 Cr in FY26.
risks_and_cash.debt_and_capex_burden: Consolidated borrowings reduced to ₹195,412 Cr in FY26. Net debt to EBITDAaL contracted to 1.3x (0.7x ex-leases). Domestic 5G rollout capex intensity has peaked and is guided 15-20% lower in FY27, driving massive Free Cash Flow generation.
risks_and_cash.margin_and_cost_pressures: Operating margins remain resilient at 57.0% quarterly OPM, enabled by the 'War on Waste' program which yielded ₹11,000 Cr+ in network opex savings over 5 years alongside SUC tax relief.
execution_and_bottlenecks: Hardware supply chain costs for AirFiber CPE equipment due to global memory/chipset price inflation.
Energy costs and diesel reliance at remote tower sites, being mitigated by solarization across 42,000+ sites.
regulatory_or_legal_headwinds: Sub-judice regulatory liabilities including AGR dues interest litigation.
Foreign exchange translation exposure in African operating markets.
risks_and_cash.source_quote: On a reported basis, net debt declined by H300,305 million year-on-year, improving Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio to 1.3x at end of March 2026 vs 2.1x at the end of March 2025.

positive_triggers: Further ARPU growth toward management's ₹300 medium-term target following full tariff hike flow-through.
Planned London listing of Airtel Money in H2 2026 unlocking value in African fintech assets.
Scaling Nxtra Data Centers toward 1 GW target, capitalizing on domestic AI and cloud hosting demand.
FCF inflection and dividend step-up following domestic 5G capex moderation.
main_risks: Currency devaluation shocks in African operating jurisdictions.
Sustained CPE price inflation slowing fixed wireless access (FWA) margin expansion.
Adverse regulatory rulings on historical DoT/AGR sub-judice levies.
what_to_watch_next: Airtel Money London IPO filing timeline and valuation benchmarks in H2 2026.
Execution pace on Nxtra 1 GW land acquisitions in Mumbai.
Net debt reduction trajectory toward net zero domestic debt.
stocker_view.investor_summary: Bharti Airtel represents a premier telecom and digital infrastructure composite exhibiting industry-leading operating metrics. Driven by continuous ARPU expansion (₹264 in Q1 FY27), record postpaid additions, and aggressive deleveraging (net debt/EBITDA down to 0.7x ex-leases), the company has entered a high free cash flow inflection phase. With audited annual operating cash flows exceeding ₹122,000 Cr and quarterly OPM sustained at 57%, Airtel is excellently positioned to fund strategic bets in Nxtra Data Centers (1 GW target) and Airtel Finance while delivering expanding return on capital (ROCE >18%) to shareholders.
